results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 33 aligned units' summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph; the five callouts are apparatus with no spec paragraph.

The outliner marked Volumes ¶2 and From the Preface to Part I ¶2. Volumes ¶2 is the spec's single 'two caveats on reading the volumes' idea (p13); conclusion ¶2 combines the takeaway and the hand-off as spec p33 declares. Neither holds an idea the spec does not assign to it.
Every unit supports MV1-MV5 or the introduction/conclusion roles; no orphan paragraph.

Each table is introduced or followed by a sentence saying what it shows (glance row 'matters most', history 'each phase left a layer', revenue shares, systems 'three facts', cast, problems, decisions, worked examples, problem-to-chapter map); each figure has an explanatory caption; the liquidity statistic is explained ('the same ratio hides very different speeds of matching').

Every declared transition_in is expressed at the start of its unit: e.g. 'That duplication comes from a history' (cause_effect), 'Veldmark runs the four businesses that history assembled' (elaboration), 'Veldmark Ads is the exception' (contrast), 'When Ingrid arrives' (time), 'Veldmark's answer to these problems' (problem_solution), 'plays the same role' (similarity), 'Smaller stories' (contrast), 'So, because' (cause_effect).

results.quote: chairs the architecture advice forum (a weekly, open meeting that gives advice rather than approvals, set up in April 2027 as part of Common Ground, below)
results.finding: The forum is defined in the cast table and then defined again almost word for word in The Common Ground Program ¶3; reader A wondered whether there were two forums. Name it here and define it once, in the governance paragraph.
results.corroborated_by: reader B (flow), item 6; reader A (flow), item 7 reported the same repeated definition

results.quote: from the bikes split (new bike categories) to AI listing tools
results.finding: 'The bikes split' is used as a known name in the cast table and explained only in the decision table (1 Nov 2027) two sections later; both readers stopped on it.

results.quote: Four identity systems, four trust-and-safety stacks, three search engines, three clouds, four product catalogs, three data warehouses.
results.finding: The counts do not reconcile with the systems table just above: it has no product-catalog row, and its trust-and-safety row shows three brands plus a dash for Keybridge. Both readers went back to the table and could not find 'four product catalogs'. Make the table and the list agree, or say which four.
results.corroborated_by: reader B (flow), item 8; reader A (flow), item 5 reported the same mismatch

results.quote: The dated decisions the chapters rely on, by date. They fall into Common Ground's four plateaus, one per year: 2027 govern and decide, 2028 move, 2029 retire and 2030 harvest (Figure 5, after the table).
results.finding: The lead-in is a fragment, and the four plateaus are introduced in passing before a long table with their figure after it; both readers re-read it, and reader B notes Figure 5's caption adds a rule ('each must leave every marketplace working on its own') the text never states. Write a full sentence that introduces the table and the plateaus.
results.corroborated_by: reader B (flow), item 10; reader A (flow), item 8 reported the same fragment and plateau placement

results.quote: Its chapters follow one €240 listing through a dozen systems in about 24 hours and add what the table leaves out, because each chapter uncovers a different weakness in almost every system the bike passes through
results.finding: The 'because' does not state a cause: uncovering weaknesses does not explain why chapters add to the table. Both readers re-read the sentence to find the logic.
results.corroborated_by: reader B (flow), item 12; reader A (flow), item 10 reported the same sentence

results.draft_locus: From the Preface to Part I ¶2
results.quote: So, because the book's failures happen at boundaries and Common Ground shares platforms beneath the products, every chapter's opening scene is one more view of a group you already know, and each chapter explains a decision about a boundary, such as which part of a capability the brands share, not a product choice.
results.finding: The cause supports only the second consequence (each chapter explains a boundary decision), not the first (each scene is a view of a known group); two conclusions are joined by 'and' under one 'because'. Reader A called it the hardest sentence on the page and read it three times. The spec's p33 phrasing has the same shape, but the draft can split the sentence while keeping the declared cause_effect transition.
results.corroborated_by: reader B (flow), item 14; reader A (flow), item 11 reported the same sentence

results.quote: Veldmark Ads is the exception to "four of everything": one ad stack
results.finding: 'Four of everything' is quoted as an established label before the body introduces it (problem 1 and Figure 3 come later). One reader only.

results.finding: Reader A had to re-count to reconcile 'two clouds' and 'a third cloud' with the 'three clouds' stated elsewhere (and the Amsterdam co-located data center in the table). One reader only.

results.draft_locus: The Recurring Worked Examples ¶1 (Rotterdam bike row)
results.quote: Femke lists a used city bike for **€240** on **Sunday 7 March 2027 at 19:42 CET**.
results.finding: The bike row is one very long cell with about fifteen timestamps; reader A read it twice to separate the Sunday listing-and-phishing story from the Monday sale and Tuesday e-mails. One reader only.

results.draft_locus: The Common Ground Program ¶5 (decision table, Jun 2027 row)
results.finding: The only decision-table entry with no indication of what it decided. One reader only.

The does_not_know terms are given or avoided: liquidity is glossed ('how fast a listing meets a buyer'), DSA spelled out, VIN, DMS, AVM, DVF, GMV, KYB, p95 and perceptual hash expanded; no learning to rank, percolation, hybrid retrieval, DAC7 or P2B appear. Flow readers flagged scenario names (bikes split, Ranking policy v1), recorded under flow_is_followable, not domain terms.
Opens with a direct statement of why the book uses one fictional group and why the alternatives fail; no placeholder, dictionary, dawn-of-man or book-report opening.

The conclusion synthesizes the three preface pages, calls back to the general-manager scene, gives a course of action and hands off to Part I; it does not open with 'In conclusion', merely restate the thesis or introduce a new subtopic.

'The three preface pages make one argument at three sizes' joins the liquidity claim, the patterns and Veldmark; the so-what (each scene is a view of a known group, each chapter a boundary decision) is stated, though its sentence is hard to parse (recorded under flow_is_followable).

'The introduction's general-manager scene returns with names attached: the six minutes to searchable is Veldmark's problem 2, and the sold bike in Tuesday's alert e-mails is Femke's €240 city bike in 214 of them.' matches the spec's callback.

The intro reader predicted the five promised groups in the roadmap's order (glance and history; brands and volumes; systems and people; eight problems and Common Ground; worked examples and chapter use) plus a closing on the preface, invented but consistent figures in tables, and a declarative briefing tone.

The reader named four problems with the expected patterns (Four of everything - Deal-Shaped Architecture; Six weeks for a category - Category Straitjacket and Attribute Junkyard; Duplicates at Hearthly - Seeing Double; Payment-link phishing - Fast Mail for Fraudsters), plus Overlap in Poland as a fifth.
The reader confirmed €225 and Monday 8 March 2027, corrected the buyer fee to €11.95 (5% x €225 + €0.70) and the reservation time to 14:02, as expected.
